{{short description|Situation in which there are contradictory ways of reducing a mathematical  expression}}
In [[mathematics]], [[computer science]] and [[logic]], '''overlap''', as a property of the reduction rules in [[term rewriting system]], describes a situation where a number of different reduction rules specify potentially contradictory ways of reducing a reducible expression, also known as a redex, within a [[Term (logic)|term]].<ref>{{cite book | title=Term Rewriting Systems | author1=Marc Bezem |author2=Jan Willem Klop |author3=Roel de Vrijer | series=Cambridge Tracts in Theoretical Computer Science | publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] | year=2003 | isbn=0-521-39115-6 | page=48|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7QQ5u-4tRUkC |location=Cambridge, UK }}</ref>

More precisely, if a number of different reduction rules share function symbols on the left-hand side, overlap can occur. Often we do not consider trivial overlap with a redex and itself.

==Examples==

Consider the term rewriting system defined by the following reduction rules:
: <math>\rho_1\ :\ f(g(x), y) \rightarrow y</math>
: <math>\rho_2\ :\ g(x) \rightarrow f(x, x)</math>

The term  <math>f(g(x), y)</math> can be reduced via &rho;<sub>1</sub> to yield {{math|''y''}}, but it can also be reduced via &rho;<sub>2</sub> to yield <math>f(f(x, x), y).</math>. Note how the redex  <math>g(x)</math> is contained in the redex <math>f(g(x), y)</math>. The result of reducing different redexes is described in a what is known as a [[Critical pair (logic)|critical pair]]; the critical pair arising out of this term rewriting system is <math>(f(f(x, x), y), y)</math>.

Overlap may occur with fewer than two reduction rules.

Consider the term rewriting system defined by the following reduction rule:
: <math> \rho_1\ :\ g(g(x)) \rightarrow x</math>
The term <math>g(g(g(x)))</math> has overlapping redexes, which can be either applied to the innermost occurrence or to the outermost occurrence of the <math>g(g(x))</math> term.
